bio: Yamazato made history when, thanks to Masanori Tomikawa's subtle cuisine that is full of velvet-smooth flavours, it became the first traditional kaiseki restaurant outside Japan to be awarded a MICHELIN star. The chef displays his incredible technique, for example, by serving thinly sliced sea bream sashimi or a deceptively simple salad that contains a whirlwind of nuances. Frequently flown in from Japan, the ingredients are showcased in their purest form. This place is all about the depth of the flavours. For instance, half a persimmon is hollowed out and stuffed with small cubes of the fruit along with Japanese scallops and maitake mushroom.The chef then tops it with a gratinated silky mousse of egg, lotus root and dashi.
